items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: The interviewee addresses the interviewer as 'Dick' multiple times (e.g., 'Yeah, Dick get a deck, yeah?', 'Okay, Dick.') and shares personal information (moving house) and asks about the interviewer's whereabouts, indicating a personal acquaintance.

ctx.x: I never have played Tunk, man. I wish I had a deck of cotch.
Or Coom Can, I've never played Coom Can. Yeah, Dick get a deck, yeah?
Yeah, we'll get us some decks, and we'll learn how to play those games, because I think all that, people ought to know that, you know?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: The interviewee addresses the interviewer as 'Dick' throughout the transcript (e.g., 'Well, Dick, you got me there'). The 'PERSON TO JUDGE' is identified as 'Dick Allen', who introduces himself as 'Dick Allen is my name' in the transcript. The interviewee's relationship is with the interviewer, not

ctx.x: What about other trumpet players down here? Did any of them feature long phrases, you know, where they would take a breath every four bars, every eight bars, or something like that?

Well, Dick, you got me there. I wouldn't know because we didn't use two trumpets in the same one band here then. Sometime like a tuxedo band, they would use two trumpets sometimes. But the average band we had them days, they said one trumpet, ain't nobody to take breath with you. Just play your own way, you know what I mean? And amateurs for that. I had a bad way of starting off, but I changed. See, I used to play inside of my lip. And then I put the horn on the outside, but then I could catch the notes I wanted,…
Well, I play it like this now. And that's the standard. Yeah. Now who plays around inside of the lip way today? I see somebody doing that not long ago.
